# opwan_tunnels (Data Source)

Every tunnel of the account, by number. Each has its own plan, type, usage and configuration.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "opwan_tunnels" "all" {}

output "tunnel_ids" {
  value = { for t in data.opwan_tunnels.all.tunnels : t.name => t.id }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Read-Only

- `max_tunnels` (Number) How many tunnels an account may have.
- `tunnels` (Attributes List) The tunnels, by number. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tunnels))

<a id="nestedatt--tunnels"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tunnels`

Read-Only:

- `addresses` (List of String) The addresses routed down this tunnel, as /32s.
- `allowance_bytes` (Number) The account's data this month, pooled across its tunnels.
- `allowed_ips` (List of String) Suggested `AllowedIPs` of the peer on the client. Empty for L2TP/IPsec.
- `bgp` (Attributes) Customer BGP over this tunnel, in brief. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tunnels--bgp))
- `created_at` (String) When the tunnel was created (RFC 3339).
- `customer_endpoint` (String) The registered fixed public IPv4 (L2TP/IPsec over IKEv1).
- `endpoint` (String) The exit's WireGuard endpoint, `host:port`. Null for L2TP/IPsec.
- `id` (String) The tunnel id (`tun_...`).
- `ike` (String) `ikev2` or `ikev1` for L2TP/IPsec, else null.
- `ipsec_id` (String) The IKEv2 identity the router sends (its local ID).
- `ipsec_server_id` (String) opwan's IKE identity, the router's remote ID.
- `l2tp_username` (String) The L2TP user name, null for WireGuard.
- `location` (String) The tunnel's location id.
- `mtu` (Number) Suggested client MTU.
- `name` (String) The tunnel's name, shown in the dashboard.
- `number` (Number) 1, 2, ... in the account.
- `peak_mbps` (Number) The speed ceiling in effect, Mbps.
- `persistent_keepalive` (Number) Suggested `PersistentKeepalive` in seconds. Null for L2TP/IPsec.
- `plan` (String) `base` or `plus`.
- `public_key` (String) The client's WireGuard public key, null for L2TP/IPsec or before one is set.
- `server` (String) The host name the router connects to.
- `server_public_key` (String) The exit's WireGuard public key, null until the exit has reported it, and for L2TP/IPsec.
- `state` (String) `pending_payment`, `setup_required` (a WireGuard tunnel without a key yet), `active`, `suspended` or `canceled`.
- `status` (Attributes) The tunnel's live state, as the exit last reported it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tunnels--status))
- `type` (String) `wireguard` or `l2tp_ipsec`.
- `used_bytes` (Number) This tunnel's share of the month's data, both directions.

<a id="nestedatt--tunnels--bgp"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tunnels.bgp`

Read-Only:

- `asn` (Number) The account's AS number, null until the account first turns BGP on.
- `enabled` (Boolean) BGP is on.
- `export` (String) `default` or `full`, null while BGP is off.
- `state` (String) `established`, `connecting`, `down`, `limit` or `disabled`; null while BGP is off or before the first report.


<a id="nestedatt--tunnels--status"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tunnels.status`

Read-Only:

- `last_handshake` (String) The last WireGuard handshake (RFC 3339), null before the first.
- `rate_bps_rx` (Number) Bits per second to you, over the last report.
- `rate_bps_tx` (Number) Bits per second from you, over the last report.
- `throttled` (String) Why the speed is lowered right now: `none`, `burst`, `allowance` or `pacing`.
- `up` (Boolean) A handshake within the last 3 minutes.
- `updated_at` (String) When the exit last reported (RFC 3339), null before the first report.
